quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does it mean when double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow traffic light ahead?

options.text: Stop completely at the intersection.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Slow down and look both ways before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and look both ways before proceeding.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and proceed with caution. Slow down and check for traffic before continuing through the intersection.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and cars are passing you on both sides. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On an expressway with four or more lanes, use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic flow, move to the right lane.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and see an emergency vehicle with its siren and lights on. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull to the right and stop before entering the intersection.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or siren, continue through and then pull to the right to let it pass. You must yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
You should increase your following distance as you drive faster.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the risk of fatal crashes. As you drive faster, you need more distance to stop, so you should increase your following distance.

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:

options.text: The same as on a dry road.
Greater than on a dry road.
Shorter than on a dry road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Greater than on a dry road.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, your vehicle takes longer to stop. Keep a greater distance from the car ahead to give yourself time to stop safely.

questions.question: You and another driver reach a four-way stop at the same time. The other car is on your left. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You go first.
Whoever signals a turn first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Construction or road work is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction or road work is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs warn you of construction, maintenance, or utility work. They help you drive safely through work zones. Fines for traffic violations double in these areas.

questions.question: When exiting an interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: Halfway through the exit ramp.
Before you enter the exit ramp.
As soon as you enter the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: As soon as you enter the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Keep your interstate speed until you enter the exit ramp. Then reduce speed to match the posted advisory speed for the ramp.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual activity:

options.text: Slows down traffic.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents or unusual sights (rubbernecking). This practice causes traffic jams and slows everyone down.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, what should you do?

options.text: You should still wear your seat belt.
You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You should wear your seat belt behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should still wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Airbags are safety devices that help protect you in crashes. For the best protection, always wear both your lap and shoulder belts along with airbags.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Turn on your signal before you reach the intersection.
Point your front wheels to the left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always signal about 100 feet before you turn left. Keep your front wheels straight ahead until it is safe to turn. This keeps you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Speeding is very dangerous. As your speed increases, crashes become more severe and cause more injury and death. Leave more space between cars as you drive faster so you can stop safely if needed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road ahead has many curves. Slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams will reflect off of water and cause glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that should be used with low beams.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic light.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer, even if they tell you to do something different than what a sign, signal, or road marking says.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check for traffic beside and behind your car.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic control signs in work zones.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use your inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas around your car. There are blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Eating, drinking coffee, or anything else cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: If a motorist sees pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should the motorist do?

options.text: Continue ahead. The motorist has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before driving through.

questions.question: You should not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles take longer to stop than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic that is large enough for you to safely merge. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards or changes in the road ahead, such as curves, steep hills, or other dangerous conditions.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light lets you proceed through the intersection. Yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder immediately when it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in rainy weather to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast causes tires to lose contact with the road and makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease as vehicle speed increases.
Are not affected by vehicle speed.
Increase as vehicle speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase as vehicle speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and stay stopped until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a full stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with any amount of alcohol in your blood. Is this true?

options.text: Only if your blood alcohol level is 0.15 percent or more.
Only if your blood alcohol level is 0.08 percent or more.
Yes, any amount of alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, any amount of alcohol.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. If police find any trace of alcohol, you will face serious penalties. Your license will be suspended for two years.

questions.question: What should you do before you start the car?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Do both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both A and B.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, develop a habit. Buckle your own safety belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: Roads become slippery when it first starts to rain. What should you do?

options.text: Do not turn or stop quickly while driving fast.
Test your tire grip by driving uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of far ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn or stop quickly while driving fast.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. You must drive slower on wet roads than dry roads. To avoid skidding, do not make quick turns or sudden stops.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Let all other traffic pass before you cross.
Stop completely, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not take up much space.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Completely move into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Completely move into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle its own full lane when you pass. Never share a lane with a motorcycle. If you return to your lane too soon, the rider may have to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: In which situation should you NOT point your wheels straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
When parked on the side of a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
questions.explanation: While waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight. If a car hits you from behind, this keeps you from sliding into oncoming traffic. On hills or slopes, turn your wheels so your car will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way rules.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can harm your ability to drive safely. Even a small amount affects your judgment and body control. Driving after drinking any amount of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into the truck's blind spots or are so close the driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Areas where cars have enough space behind the truck.
Areas where cars have several car lengths of space between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into the truck's blind spots or are so close the driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where a car is too close and blocks the truck driver from stopping or turning safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.
Look for another train coming.
Do both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both A and B.
questions.explanation: Even after a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not move until all gates are up and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: This sign warns that the road ahead:

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves only to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a reverse curve. The road curves to the right first, then to the left.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a constant speed.
Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Drive with caution near railroad tracks.

questions.question: How do you avoid glare from headlights of an oncoming car?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Focus on the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. Then look ahead to check where the other car is.

questions.question: What can speed up the process of alcohol leaving your body?

options.text: Nothing. Only time removes all alcohol from your body.
Taking a cold shower.
Eating a large meal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing. Only time removes all alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes about 90 percent of alcohol from your body. Alcohol leaves at about one drink per hour. Nothing can speed this up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars on the right go first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let other traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: This sign means yield. Slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians cross your path before you proceed. Stop if needed.

questions.question: How do you see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Check only the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Check only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Stop.
Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What is a driving distraction?

options.text: Anything that makes you take evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?

options.text: Breathe fresh air.
Give your body time.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol works quickly but leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower blood alcohol content. Waiting is the only way to lower it.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: Your reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision and makes you less alert. More alcohol means worse judgment and worse driving. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and other vehicles.
